tagline: A phone snap becomes a product image you can use.
brief: Product concept: a photo editor for small online sellers. Turn an ordinary phone photo into a clean product image, compare backgrounds, and export a version for a listing or social post.
promise: Turn a phone photo into a cleaner product image
question: How can the same product prove the improvement before the feature explanation?
overview: Three source demonstrations show a visible input, editing steps, and a finished product image. Lead with the before and after, keep the object recognizable, then show enough of the workflow to make the change understandable. Product photos is an illustrative product concept, not a claim about a released app. Source views and interactions describe the indexed posts; they do not establish sales, conversion, organic reach, or editing accuracy.
searchNotes: Reuse-first research followed by compact caption and transcript searches. Full detail was reserved for finalists.
All 24 gokceercan, 32 photoshop._blog, and 33 spk3241_ indexed frames were visually inspected. These references show real people or hands and are not people-free examples.
spk3241_ has a Thai caption and unrelated song transcript. Its relevance comes from the inspected interface and product frames, not a translated testimonial.
Promotional captions and discount codes are retained as source evidence. The suggested storyboard makes no time-saving or sales guarantee.

angles.title: Let the same object prove the change.
angles.label: BEFORE AND AFTER
angles.description: Open with the original snap beside the edited result. Keep the crop and object recognizable so the viewer can judge the improvement.
angles.whyItFits: A seller can see what the editor changes before hearing a feature list.
angles.evidence: gokceercan compares the same bag at 3.2s. spk3241_ shows a grey-surface toothbrush at 3.93s and the white-background output at 21.13s. No sales outcome is measured.
angles.suggestedHook: Same product. Which photo would you put in your listing?
angles.visualDirection: Start with a labeled original and edited image. Keep product details visible and use actual app output.

angles.title: Replace the setup montage with a visible workflow.
angles.label: SHOW THE STEPS
angles.description: Show the inconvenient starting photo, then import, edit, compare, and export. Finish on the usable image.
angles.whyItFits: The workflow explains the proposed product through an observable task.
angles.evidence: photoshop._blog shows props before Product Staging at 15.37s. gokceercan shows import at 12.6s, background editing at 14.8s, and a share view at 21.8s.
angles.suggestedHook: Start with the photo you already have.
angles.visualDirection: One original photo stays in view while the actual editing steps produce a new background. Avoid invented processing-time counters.

tagline: Compare the change before you change the room.
brief: Product concept: an interior preview tool that compares furniture and decor choices in a room. Show the difference with diagrams, rendered rooms, or screen recordings. Creative constraint: no people or faces on screen; hands and fingers are allowed.
promise: Compare decor choices before committing to one
question: How can a furniture comparison make the benefit visible without filming a person?
overview: Three references fit the sampled evidence when hands and fingers are allowed. An empty-to-furnished room reveal provides direct product-style proof; furniture and floor-plan comparisons provide adjacent creative mechanisms. A presenter-led reference remains excluded, and a thumbnail-only source remains uncertain. These are indexed samples, not a guarantee about every moment of each video. Room preview is an illustrative product concept.
searchNotes: The no-person rule allows hands and fingers, as clarified by the user. Three references fit the inspected sample, one is excluded and one remains uncertain.
Kit & Kaboodle has ten inspected indexed frames; its empty room at 7.9s becomes furnished at 11.6s.
Planner5D supplies furniture comparisons (three indexed frames) and floor-plan comparisons (seven indexed frames). These mechanisms are not proof of an app workflow.
mavgpt remains excluded because a presenter is visible. The bedroom source has no indexed frames and remains uncertain rather than being accepted from its thumbnail.
Only sampled evidence was inspected, not continuous video. Views and interactions do not establish causal performance or conversions.

angles.title: Make the preview the reveal.
angles.label: VISIBLE TRANSFORMATION
angles.description: Show the current room, then the decor preview from the same viewpoint. Hands can hold the phone; let the changed room carry the reveal.
angles.whyItFits: The viewer sees what comparing decor choices changes before hearing a feature explanation.
angles.evidence: Kit & Kaboodle shows an empty room at 7.9s and a furnished room at 11.6s. The phone is held in hands, which are allowed.
angles.suggestedHook: Before you move anything, see what changes.
angles.visualDirection: Use an actual room image and a supported preview of the same room. Keep faces and presenters out of frame; hands operating the interface are allowed.

angles.title: Change one detail. Let the viewer compare.
angles.label: PEOPLE-FREE COMPARISON
angles.description: Place two versions of the same furnishing arrangement together. Change the lighting or furniture scale while keeping the rest recognizable.
angles.whyItFits: A room-preview concept can explain its benefit through the images alone.
angles.evidence: The furniture comparison source contrasts lighting at 2.2s, bedside furniture at 3.8s and TV-console scale at 7.0s. The floor-plan source adds a schematic side-by-side mechanism with pointing fingers.
angles.suggestedHook: Same room. Which version would you choose?
angles.visualDirection: Use actual screen recordings or rendered comparisons. Hands may point at choices. Keep faces and presenters out of frame, and label options A and B without claiming universal correctness.
